speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: asked 	the Minister for National Development (a) how many current HDB flat lessees concurrently own one or more private residential properties; (b) of these, how many are not living in their HDB flats; (c) whether there are any plans to review the policy of allowing HDB flat lessees to keep their HDB flats after they become private property owners; and (d) if not, what other plans does the Ministry have to increase the supply of resale HDB flats and thus moderate their prices.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Another 4% of HDB flat owners are renting out one or more bedrooms of their HDB flat.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These proportions have stayed stable in the last three years.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Among the remaining 97% of the flat owners who do not own private residential property, about 13% are renting out their whole flat or bedrooms within their flat.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This proportion has also stayed stable in the last three years.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We note that Mr Gerald Giam is asking the Government to consider requiring HDB flat owners to sell their HDB flats, or dispose their HDB flats, if they buy private property.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: So, this has put resale flats beyond the reach of many Singaporeans, even after factoring in the generous Government grants.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: The purpose of my question was to discuss ways to moderate resale flat prices, so they are more affordable for lower- and middle-income Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: And one way to achieve this is to increase the supply of resale flats.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: So, since HDB flats are meant for owner occupation, can HDB owners who buy private property in the future be required to sell their flats so that the flats are freed up to be bought by other Singaporeans?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I note that the Minister has said that this is under discussion and I appreciate that.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Because this will be consistent with the current rule which requires private property owners who buy an HDB flat to dispose their private property within six months of the flat purchase.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I have given the Member the proportion of HDB flat owners who concurrently hold private property as well as HDB flats.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And of those who rent out their HDB flats, it is a smaller subset of that.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Having said that, I have given the Member a reply that we study all options and possibilities.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Members know that we do not discuss cooling measures, other than those that have already been issued.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For resale flat prices, the Member is right.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are also mindful of macroeconomic conditions going forward: rising interest rates, uncertainty in the economic climate globally, people being more prudent in their home purchases.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, those will also have an impact and we will need to monitor the market carefully.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Member repeats the point about million-dollar flats.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Indeed, these headline-grabbing prices have caused concern and fuelled market psychology, causing people to worry, and then, hence, go into the market.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I think the Member is aware: they tend to be jumbo flats, loft units, high floors, larger units, executive apartments, maisonettes, the 3-room type HDB flats that are legacy terrace houses.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Nevertheless, with grants as well as the measures we are putting in place, we want to make sure that the property market remains in line with economic fundamentals.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have said before, numerous times, we will act decisively but carefully to ensure that the property market remains in line with economic fundamentals.
